name: Gautam Adani
title: The Diamond Sorter Who Built India's Gateways
subtitle: From sorting diamonds at 16 to India's richest man, with every win and every controversy on the record.
hook: On New Year's Day ==1998==, gunmen seized Gautam Adani at gunpoint as he drove away from a club in Ahmedabad. He was freed the next day. Asked about it on television 25 years later, he said: __"I slept well that very night."__ Ten years after the kidnapping he was dining at the Taj in Mumbai when the 26/11 attack began, and he spent that night trapped inside the hotel.

glance.label: Born
glance.value: 24 June 1962, in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, into a Gujarati Jain family

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: The dry north of Gujarat in Banaskantha, then Ahmedabad for four years of secondary school

glance.label: Education
glance.value: Gave up formal education at 16, in 1978. A Mumbai college, Jai Hind, rejected his application around then. In 2023 he said he regrets not finishing college.

glance.label: First job
glance.value: Learning to sort diamonds at Mahendra Brothers in Mumbai, at 16. A cousin got him in.

glance.label: First company
glance.value: His own diamond brokerage at Zaveri Bazaar, Mumbai, while still a teenager. Adani Exports followed in 1988, when he was about 26.

glance.label: Main company today
glance.value: Founder and chairman of the Adani Group, based in Ahmedabad. Adani Enterprises is its flagship.

glance.label: Source of wealth
glance.value: Commodities and infrastructure, self-made. Forbes put him at ==$112.7 billion== on 30 September 2026, as India's richest. Bloomberg's index briefly ranked him the world's second-richest in September 2022, at about $146.8 billion.

glance.label: Family
glance.value: Married to Dr Priti Adani, who founded and chairs the Adani Foundation. Two sons work in the group: Karan runs Adani Ports as Managing Director, and Jeet is a Director at Adani Airports.

glance.label: Known for
glance.value: Mundra Port, eight airports and a big green-energy bet. Also two storms: Hindenburg's 2023 allegations, which the group denied and which India's regulator said in 2025 could not be established; and a US criminal case, dismissed by a judge in August 2026 after prosecutors asked to drop it.

contact.howToReach: We found no personal email or phone number that Gautam Adani has published, so treat anyone selling you one as a scam. If you are a founder, the door built for you is Vande Bharatam, his innovation programme: it accepts a concept, prototype or running business and needs no registered start-up, though its first finale was in August 2026, so check the site to see what is open now. For anything else, write to the team that owns your topic: investor relations for shareholders, corporate communications for journalists only, the Adani Foundation for community work, and careers.adani.com for jobs, where the group warns it never asks candidates for money. Cold calls to the switchboard and letters addressed to the chairman are, in our judgement, unlikely to reach him, and his social accounts are for reading his views rather than pitching him. Keep any message under 120 words: who you are, one specific thing you have built with a real number, and the one thing you are asking for.

factCheck.method: Contact channels and social accounts were read from the organisations' own contact, investor and profile pages, their press releases and a stock-exchange filing; none came from contact-finder sites. Gautam Adani's three personal accounts are linked from his official Adani Group profile; we did not confirm a platform verification badge on each. Vande Bharatam's email and missed-call number come from its website's footer code, because the page text would not load for our reader. The hook rests on PTI's report of the police charge sheet, Outlook Business's PTI report and India TV's English transcript of his January 2023 Aap Ki Adalat interview; the interview quote is as printed in that transcript, and we did not check it against the broadcast. Reuters' article on the US dismissal was read only as a search excerpt, so CBS News and the court order carry the detail. Photo licences and authors come from the Commons API, and each chosen photo was viewed. Our web-search allowance ran out near the end, so the last checks used known pages only.

disputed.note: PTI (2018), citing the charge sheet, dates the abduction to 1 January 1998. Outlook Business reports a demand of USD 1.5-2 million and says it is not known whether any ransom was paid; another outlet gives Rs 15 crore paid and dates it to 1997. We state no ransom. In court, six accused were acquitted in 2005 and two more in 2018 on benefit of doubt, with witnesses unable to identify them and Adani not appearing to give a further statement. Nobody named by these reports was convicted.

disputed.claim: "15 feet" from death at the Taj
disputed.note: Outlook Business quotes him in 2008 saying he saw death at 15 feet. It is not in the India TV transcript we read, so we left it out of the hook.

disputed.claim: Which index ranked him world's second-richest
disputed.note: CBS (via WTOP) and Outlook Business cite Bloomberg's index, about $146.8-147 billion, September 2022. Search excerpts also say Forbes's real-time list briefly placed him second, near $153-154 billion, but we could not open a page to confirm it, so we cite Bloomberg's.

disputed.claim: When the US criminal case ended
disputed.note: Indian outlets reported in May 2026 that the case was closed permanently, when the Justice Department moved to drop it. The court only dismissed the counts against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain, with prejudice, on 10 August 2026. Judge Garaufis granted this while writing that irregularities in the decision were concerning, and reserved judgment on other counts against five other defendants; we did not check what happened to those after the 31 August deadline. Separately, PTI reported Gautam Adani agreed to pay USD 6 million to settle the SEC civil case, without admitting or denying wrongdoing; we could not confirm final court approval. The group has rejected the allegations throughout.
Forbes calls him a college dropout. His own account, reported by PTI and DT Next, is that he gave up education at 16 and moved to Mumbai. We follow his words.
He said about three years in his 2023 speech (PTI). PTI's 2024 Jai Hind report says about two. Since he also says he returned to Ahmedabad at 19, the glance gives no length.
His official profile says twelve; the group's site menu lists ten. We give no number.

disputed.claim: Press email on the Adani Green newsroom page
disputed.note: The page displays media@adani.com, but the link behind it opens mediainfo@adaniports.com. We could not tell which is live, so neither is listed. We list the media contact printed on the group's October 2026 press release instead.

The Kerry photo's description says January 2014, but its capture date is 11 January 2015 and it names the 7th Vibrant Gujarat Summit, so we use 2015. The portrait is dated 26 January 2012 on Commons, but it comes from a photo with Ambassador Timothy Roemer who, from general knowledge not re-checked here, left the post in 2011. The year is left null.

'Secretary Rubio Meets with Adani Group' (2026) actually shows N. Chandrasekaran of Tata, so the State Department labels look swapped. 'Gautam Adani.jpg' is a clear front-facing portrait, but its source reads 'was sent to me personally' with Adani as author, which is weak proof of the licence. 'Adani Mundra Port Kutch Gujarat.jpg' is a 500-pixel image that looks like a stock shot, and we could not confirm it shows Mundra. GODL-India-only files were skipped as outside our licence list.
